name: Gen 2 - R2-D2 blue / Naboo, 72 segments (layout unverified)
verification_note: Read off Coordinates(blue).pdf with tools/extract_label_pads.py, which reproduces the Gen-1 layout exactly from the green drawing, so its readings here are trustworthy. 56 of the 72 label pads are in the same place on both plates; 16 are not. FOUR ARE A STRUCTURAL CHANGE: segments 51 and 52 move from column 10 (rows 9 and 12) to column 18, rows 1 and 20, and segments 57 and 58 from column 36 (rows 9 and 12) to column 28, rows 1 and 20 - that is, out of the vertical edge strips and onto the top and bottom edge rows across the middle of the plate, which the green plate does not have. THE OTHER TWELVE ARE ONE PAD OVER: 38, 41, 49, 54, 55, 60, 68 and 71 shift by one column and 39, 40, 69 and 70 by one row, which is what a two-pad-wide edge strip and a different row split would look like. None of that fixes the boundaries: a label pad marks where a number is printed, not where a segment ends, and on this board the segments are formed by routing pads to shunts, so the boundaries are in the netlist rather than in any drawn outline - Layers_Black_White(blue).pdf shows pads, routing and ground planes, not segment zones. Until the pad-to-segment mapping comes from the KiCad board file or a segment/pad-list table, this file carries the Gen-1 tiling: right for the 56 segments whose labels did not move, wrong for at least the four that changed region. Correct the rectangles below, then set verified to true.
notes: Pad grid, plate size and segment count are certain from Coordinates(blue).pdf: 45 x 20 pads of 5.6 x 6.05 mm = 900 pads over 252.0 x 121.0 mm, 72 segments, temperature sensors at x = 0, 84, 168, 252 mm. The Naboo calibration campaign confirms 72 segment channels and 4 sensors.
